summary: Rebecca foresees her death and asks Jacob to honor Isaac and Esau, then presses Isaac about the danger she believes Esau still poses. Despite Isaac's distrust, she obtains promises of brotherly love from both sons and asks to be buried near Sarah; she dies that night, and Jacob and Esau bury her together.
whyItMatters: Rebecca's last acts aim to preserve family peace beyond her death. The chapter holds her hope for mutual love beside Isaac's ominous prediction that Esau will not keep his oath.

context.author: In the book's Sinai frame an angel recounts this material to Moses. That narrative speaker is distinct from the historical author, whom this chapter does not identify.
context.audience: Moses receives the account inside the story for Israel and its descendants. The historical work addresses Jewish concerns about covenant, inherited stories, and observance; a specific first community is uncertain.
context.date: The narrative uses a chronology counted from creation within its Sinai revelation frame. The historical work is usually placed in the second century BCE; an exact composition date is not established.
context.setting: Rebecca and Isaac's household during Rebecca's final conversations with her husband and twin sons.
context.literaryForm: Farewell narrative with a dream announcement, contrasting character judgments, sworn promises, and burial.

before.text: Joseph has been sold, Jacob is grieving, and the family has suffered further deaths. The narrative now returns to Rebecca's effort to secure peace between her own sons.

here.text: Rebecca's petition moves from Jacob to Isaac to Esau, ending in reciprocal promises and a shared meal before her death.

after.text: Isaac's own farewell repeats the demand for brotherly love and addresses the disputed birthright before his death.

outline.heading: Rebecca announces her approaching death
outline.note: She asks Jacob to honor his family and tells him the dream that revealed her death; he doubts her because she is strong.

outline.heading: Rebecca petitions Isaac
outline.note: She contrasts Esau’s conduct with Jacob’s provision and asks for an oath against violence.

outline.heading: Isaac’s distrust and prediction
outline.note: Isaac praises Jacob, condemns Esau, and says an attack will end in Esau’s defeat.

outline.heading: Esau promises love and burial
outline.note: Rebecca asks for peace and burial near Sarah, and Esau swears to love Jacob.

outline.heading: Jacob’s promise and Rebecca’s burial
outline.note: Jacob also pledges love, and the brothers bury their mother after her death that night.

keyVerses.text: And she said unto him: 'I ask you that the day I die, thou wilt take me in and bury me near Sarah, thy father's mother, and that thou and Jacob will love each other and that neither will desire evil against the other, but mutual love only, and (so) ye will prosper, my sons, and be honoured in the midst of the land, and no enemy will rejoice over you, and ye will be a blessing and a mercy in the eyes of all those that love you.'
keyVerses.why: Rebecca combines her burial request with a concrete appeal for mutual love and an end to hostile intent.

keyVerses.text: And Jacob, my brother, also, I shall love above all flesh; for I have not a brother in all the earth but him only: and this is no great merit for me if I love him; for he is my brother, and we were sown together in thy body, and together came we forth from thy womb, and if I do not love my brother, whom shall I love?
keyVerses.why: Esau grounds his promise in shared brotherhood and birth from the same mother.

keyVerses.text: And they eat and drank, she and her sons that night, and she died, three jubilees and one week and one year old, on that night, and her two sons, Esau and Jacob, buried her in the double cave near Sarah, their father's mother.
keyVerses.why: The brothers jointly carry out the burial request after the final family meal.

questions.question: Why does Rebecca raise these instructions now?
questions.answer: She says a dream has revealed that she will die within the year, despite her continuing health. The instructions are therefore presented as preparation for the family's life after her death.

questions.question: Why does Jacob laugh at her prediction?
questions.answer: He sees that she remains strong, mobile, and free of the infirmity he would expect near death. His disbelief responds to that visible health, while the narrative later confirms her announced death.

questions.question: What does Rebecca ask Isaac to do?
questions.answer: She wants him to make Esau swear not to injure or pursue Jacob. Her request draws on the hostility and appropriation of parental possessions she attributes to Esau, contrasted with Jacob's continuing provision.

questions.question: Does Isaac believe an oath will change Esau?
questions.answer: No. Isaac says Esau will not keep it and predicts that an attempt to kill Jacob will lead to Esau's own defeat. The chapter leaves that prediction alongside Esau's subsequent solemn promise rather than resolving the tension immediately.

questions.question: What is meant by Jacob’s greater “guardian”?
questions.answer: Isaac speaks of a protector of Jacob who is greater and more powerful than Esau's protector. The verse does not name or further describe these guardians, so identifying them with a particular later angelic scheme would go beyond the chapter.

questions.question: How should Isaac’s condemnation of Esau’s descendants be read?
questions.answer: Isaac predicts destruction not only for Esau but for his descendants and associates that fate with abandoning Abraham's God. It is a sweeping judgment voiced in the narrative and must not be turned into a verdict on modern populations.

questions.question: What is distinctive about Esau’s answer to Rebecca?
questions.answer: He says love for Jacob is no special achievement because Jacob is his only brother and they shared her womb. He also asks that Jacob be instructed to protect him and his sons, acknowledging the imbalance created by the blessing.

questions.question: Do the sons fulfill any part of their promises before the chapter ends?
questions.answer: Both pledge love, share a meal with Rebecca, and together bury her near Sarah as requested. The shared burial is an immediate fulfillment of her wishes, even though the future durability of their peace remains unresolved here.

glossary.def: A solemn sworn commitment, used here to promise love and the absence of hostile intent toward a brother.
Isaac’s term for the protector whose greater power he says will preserve Jacob.
The ancestral burial place where Rebecca is laid near Sarah.
